articles.headline: Dodgers juggle rotation, hope for Ohtani return this week
articles.description: Los Angeles recalled Emmet Sheehan and placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list as part of a series of roster moves Sunday, with manager Dave Roberts also expressing hope that Shohei Ohtani will be back in the lineup soon.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- The Dodgers recalled pitcher Emmet Sheehan as part of a series of roster moves Sunday, with the right-hander set to handle the bulk of their series finale against the San Francisco Giants.

All four transactions involved Dodgers pitchers. They also recalled Kyle Hurt, placed Tarik Skubal on the bereavement list and optioned Seth Halvorsen to Triple-A Oklahoma City.

Jack Dreyer will start as the Dodgers go for the sweep against their Bay Area rivals before giving way to Sheehan, who is 5-8 with a 4.79 ERA in 22 games this season.

"Kind of piecing through the available options today," manager Dave Roberts said. "I think it's just more of what gives Emmet, in our opinion, the best chance."

Right fielder Kyle Tucker won't be in the lineup after coming out of Saturday's 10-4 victory because of a fouled pitch that went off his right knee. The early exit was described as precautionary, and Roberts believed it was worth giving him a day off, particularly with Tucker finding his stride after an erratic first season in Los Angeles. He is batting .429 with five homers, eight extra-base hits and 11 RBIs in his past 10 games.

The Dodgers expect to see Shohei Ohtani back soon after his first stint on the injured list since joining the team in 2024. It could come during a three-game series against the San Diego Padres that starts Tuesday night.

"Still up in the air, but that's our hope," Roberts said.

Ohtani is on the 15-day IL because of right biceps inflammation. He also has been dealing with left knee soreness for months.

Roberts believes Ohtani will be pain-free going into the last week of the regular season, with the Dodgers pushing to secure a bye to avoid the wild-card round.

"There's a difference between discomfort and pain," Roberts said. "Is it 100%? Probably not. Is it better than it was a week ago? Yes. Honestly, I think that's just a better question for Shohei to give specifics. But I do think that when he's activated, it's going to be the best physical place he's been in in quite some time."

articles.headline: Patriots starting RG Mike Onwenu carted off with ankle injury
articles.description: Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field with an ankle injury late in the first quarter against the Steelers.
articles.body:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- New England Patriots starting right guard Mike Onwenu was carted off the field with a right ankle injury late in the first quarter of Sunday's 20-3 victory over the Pittsburgh Steelers.

The injury came on a play when quarterback Drake Maye was sacked and Steelers linebacker T.J. Watt landed on the back of Onwenu's legs.

In addition to Onwenu, starting outside linebacker Dre'Mont Jones left the game in the second quarter with a shoulder injury. After initially announcing Jones' return as questionable, the Patriots ruled Jones out early in the third quarter.

Onwenu is a seven-year veteran who has the longest tenure with the Patriots after being selected in the sixth round of the 2020 draft.

Durability has been one of his calling cards, as Sunday marked his 100th career regular-season game and 92nd start. A Michigan alum, he also has played in five postseason games (four starts).

Onwenu, 28, is in the final year of his contract in 2026.

Veteran Greg Van Roten, whom the Patriots signed to a one-year, $3 million deal on Aug. 18, took over for Onwenu.

The Patriots also ruled out starting safety Craig Woodson (shoulder), reserve safety Dell Pettus (ankle) and No. 2 tight end Eli Raridon (thigh) after they sustained injuries during the game.

articles.headline: Bears' Caleb Williams leaves on cart after falling on scramble
articles.description: Bears quarterback Caleb Williams exited Sunday's game against the Minnesota Vikings with a right hamstring injury.
articles.body:
CHICAGO -- Bears quarterback Caleb Williams exited Sunday's 9-3 loss to the Minnesota Vikings with a right hamstring injury midway through the fourth quarter.

After running back Kyle Monangai converted a fourth down inside the red zone, Williams took off and ran to his left with a clear path to the end zone. His right leg appeared to give way as he was running, and he fell awkwardly to the ground.

The quarterback tried twice to get himself to his feet but could not stand without the assistance of trainers. Williams was helped to the injury tent, where he stayed for several minutes before being carted back to the locker room.

Williams sat on the cart with a towel over his head and was visibly in pain when he uncovered his face. He raised his right fist in the air and gave the crowd at Soldier Field a thumbs up before disappearing into the tunnel.

Tyson Bagent replaced Williams at quarterback. The Bears failed to score a touchdown despite running two plays inside Minnesota's 6-yard line. Cairo Santos' 23-yard field goal attempt was then blocked.

The entirety of Sunday's game was played under a steady downpour.

articles.headline: José Mourinho blasts ref, VAR: 'Two clear red cards' for Atlético Madrid
articles.description: José Mourinho blasted the referee and the VAR after Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, saying Atlético should have received "two clear red cards."
articles.body:
José Mourinho blasted the referee and the VAR after Real Madrid's 2-1 derby defeat to Atlético Madrid, saying Atlético should have received "two clear red cards" and claiming the on-field official "couldn't cope with the pressure."

Alejandro Grimaldo put Atlético ahead with a second-half penalty at the Metropolitano -- after defender Dean Huijsen was sent off for bringing down Giuliano Simeone -- before Jonathan David made it 2-0. Antonio Rüdiger pulled a late goal back as Madrid dropped to fourth in the LaLiga table.

However, Mourinho's postmatch news conference focused on two first-half incidents, when Atlético's Cristian Romero was shown a yellow card -- not a red -- for treading on Jude Bellingham's knee, while Lee Kang-in escaped punishment for a crunching challenge on Federico Valverde.

Mourinho brought printed-out photos of the two incidents into the press room to show journalists, before delivering a long, damning indictment of referee Miguel Ángel Ortiz Arias and VAR Daniel Trujillo Suárez.

"The story of the game is here," Mourinho said, holding up the images of the two challenges. "They're two clear red cards. With the difficulties we had afterwards -- with 11 versus 10 [players] -- you could imagine what it would have been like [for us] for 50 minutes with 11 versus nine.

"It's the CTA [the referee's committee]. It's all been very strange. It's a referee [Ortiz Arias] who, at 41, doesn't have international experience. I don't know why he was the referee. The poor guy came here and couldn't cope with the pressure.

"But for [the VAR] there's no pressure, at [RFEF HQ] Las Rozas there's no pressure. Or maybe there is and we don't know. That combination -- a poor referee, who's only done small games, and a VAR with a big history. Congratulations to the CTA."

Real Madrid said after the match that Valverde suffered "severe trauma to his left ankle" on the tackle by Lee and that the Uruguay international would undergo further tests to assess the severity of the injury.

Mourinho said he hadn't yet seen a replay of Huijsen's red card and went on to list a series of incidents in games involving Real Madrid, Barcelona and Atlético in recent weeks, suggesting Real's rivals had benefitted.

"The penalty at Real Sociedad [for Atlético] is laughable," Mourinho said. "The penalty for Barcelona is laughable, the non-sending off [for Barcelona] against Athletic Club. So many things together. ... I thought I'd find a different league to the one I left [in 2013], and people told me no, and they explained why. But we'll fight."

Madrid are now six points behind leaders Barcelona with seven games played, going into the international break.

"If 'they' leave us in peace, and let us compete on an even playing field, there's a long way left," Mourinho said, when asked if his team could still fight for the title.

articles.headline: Bregman leaves game after being hit in face by foul ball in on-deck circle
articles.description: Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Reds after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle.
articles.body:
CINCINNATI -- - Chicago Cubs third baseman Alex Bregman left Sunday's game against the Cincinnati Reds after being struck in the face by a foul ball while standing in the on-deck circle.

In the fourth inning, left-handed batting Michael Busch fouled off a pitch from Reds right-hander Luis Mey that struck Bregman, who immediately jogged toward the Cubs' dugout with a hand over his left eye.

Bregman was escorted by a trainer down the dugout steps and into the clubhouse, with blood visible on his face. Matt Shaw pinch hit for Bregman.

Bregman is batting .260 with 26 home runs and 88 RBIs in 152 games. He signed a $175 million, five-year free agent deal in January.

The Cubs could clinch a postseason berth with a win Sunday and a Diamondbacks loss.

articles.headline: Michael Carrick keen to find Man United positives, but there aren't many right now
articles.description: This is Man United's worst start in a Premier League season in 12 years. Is there any reason to believe a turnaround is ahead?
articles.body:
LONDON -- For Michael Carrick, the international break won't feel like much of a break at all.

The games will stop, but after Manchester United's 1-1 draw with Fulham on Sunday, the spotlight and the scrutiny will remain. It's going to be a long three weeks for United's coach.

It could have been even worse. Matheus Cunha's 89th-minute equalizer prevented a first defeat at Craven Cottage in 17 years and stopped the pressure on Carrick ramping up to another level.

After back-to-back home defeats to Manchester City and Brighton, three consecutive losses would have left United's decision-makers with some thinking to do while the players jet off to join their national teams.

As it is, a point at Fulham will at least stop the bleeding -- there's not much to shout about. Five points from five games is United's worst start to a Premier League season for more than a decade. And that's after a run of fixtures that appeared on paper to be relatively manageable.

"It's not been ideal," Carrick admitted. "I know we can do better, we need to do better at certain things. But at the same time, I'm not despondent and down because I think we're showing some good signs as well.

"I'm not playing it down. We wanted more points from it."

Though Carrick was keen to find the positives, the most damning part of the day was perhaps the assessment of his former United teammate Gary Neville. The pair played together at Old Trafford for four years, but when Fulham went ahead midway through the second half, Neville did not hold back.

"I've watched Manchester United since the age of 5," he said. "That's the worst 15 minutes I've ever seen them play."

Given some of the disastrous displays over the past decade, it was quite a statement. Neville's outburst -- during which he branded parts of the performance as "pathetic" -- was prompted by a calamitous Fulham goal.

Kobbie Mainoo's pass into midfield was telegraphed by Calvin Bassey, who was too strong for Cunha. Then the Fulham defender was allowed to advance unchallenged into the penalty area before firing a tame shot at Senne Lammens.

But when things aren't going well, even the most innocuous situations can turn into something else. This time, Bassey's shot hit Lammens before rebounding back toward the goal off Lisandro Martínez.

A scrambling Lammens chose to use his feet rather than his hands to stop the ball and succeeded only in booting it into the net. It was either bad luck or symptomatic of a United team struggling with the confidence to make decisive decisions.

Self-belief, or lack of it, is not the only issue for Carrick to address. There's a feeling among some fans that United have not looked fit enough during the early part of the season.

Running stats aren't everything, but at the end of the 90 minutes, Fulham's players had covered an extra 6 kilometers more than United's players. There were certainly times during the game when it appeared obvious that the home side was quicker, faster and sharper.

articles.headline: Saints LT Kelvin Banks Jr. carted off with ankle injury
articles.description: Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) was ruled out against the Ravens in the fourth quarter.
articles.body:
BALTIMORE -- New Orleans Saints left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) was ruled out of Sunday's game against the Baltimore Ravens in the fourth quarter.

Banks was carted off the field after landing awkwardly on his ankle on a third-and-19 play that resulted in Tyler Shough being sacked. Banks appeared to grab his left ankle and did not get up. He was attended to by the medical staff before getting on a cart and leaving the game.

The 22-year-old Banks was the ninth pick of the 2025 draft and started all 17 games at left tackle for New Orleans last season.

Veteran lineman Asim Richards took over for Banks on the next offensive series. The Dallas Cowboys traded Richards and a 2028 seventh-round pick to the Saints during the 2025 preseason in exchange for a 2028 sixth-round pick.

articles.headline: Transfer rumors, news: Liverpool, Man City eye Real Sociedad's Aramburu
articles.description: Man City and Liverpool are both looking at Real Sociedad defender Jon Aramburu. Transfer Talk has the latest.
articles.body:
Real Sociedad right-back Jon Aramburu is being looked at by Manchester City and Liverpool. Meanwhile, Real Madrid striker Endrick could be the subject of a January bid from Premier League champions Arsenal. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

Transfers home page | Men's summer grades | Women's grades

Trending rumors

- Manchester City and Liverpool are both considering a move for Real Sociedad right-back Jon Aramburu, TEAMtalk reports. The Venezuela international has been one of the defensive stars of the season in LaLiga and his form has attracted interest from a number of clubs across Europe. The 24-year-old has been particularly impressive in one-vs.-one situations while also making an impact further forward, while his ability to play on the left as well as the right makes him an attractive and versatile proposition. Aramburu's contract, which runs until 2030, has a release clause of around £50 million. 

- Arsenal are monitoring striker Endrick's situation at Real Madrid with a view to making a move in January, according to TEAMtalk. The 20-year-old Brazil international's first appearance this season came as a late substitute in Tuesday's 3-2 win at Elche, and he is concerned about his role both now and in the long term. There is a growing belief among a number of clubs -- including Liverpool, Manchester City and Manchester United -- that he could be available in 2027. Endrick doesn't want to leave, and Madrid are reluctant to part with a player in whom they have invested heavily, but the situation is complicated because of the amount of competition around him.

- Liverpool are preparing to receive bids for midfielder Florian Wirtz in January, including from Bayern Munich, though the club are reluctant to part with the 23-year-old, according to AS. Wirtz has struggled to reach his peak form on a consistent basis since arriving from Bayer Leverkusen and is without a goal in his last 12 competitive matches for club and country. As a result, clubs across Europe believe there's a chance they could tempt him away from Anfield, but Liverpool are likely to reject any advances. Reds boss Andoni Iraola still sees the Germany midfielder as a key part of his plans.

- Chelsea fear that defender Josh Acheampong could leave, AS reports. The Blues are alarmed at the amount of interest in the 20-year-old and are worried he could depart in January, despite having been given a starting role for the club, and assurances that he is part of their long-term plans by boss Xabi Alonso. The centre-back has started four games, but has been part of a defence that has conceded two goals or more a game in 2026-27.

- Real Madrid star Jude Bellingham is close to extending his contract at Real Madrid until 2032, according to Nicolò Schira. The England star's existing contract runs until 2029, but Los Blancos are keen to secure the long-term future of a player they consider one of the cornerstones of the club.
